title: CSIRO Total Well Being Diet (Weight Loss Meal Planner) 12 Month Subscription $249 @ TotalWellBeingDiet
body:
Deal: CSIRO Total Well Being Diet (Weight Loss Meal Planner) 12 Month Subscription $249 @ TotalWellBeingDiet

[M00Cow] $200 off* for a full year of support
$200 off how much amd what?
[Fitmusclebro] What's included:
Enjoy simple and delicious higher protein, low GI meal plans
Keep on track by recording your food and exercise
Online Group Coaching sessions to help you on your journey
Stay motivated with a supportive, caring community
(Optional)
Follow a condition-specific program for pre-diabetes/type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure, high cholesterol or joint pain
Menopause Plan
[WatchNerd] Or just use Ai to do the same thing for free.
[M00Cow] yeah its not hard.
Keep a food diary, you'll soon realise how much crap you eat.
[Jimothy Wongingtons] Not me logging 1 pack of Tim tams as 1 Tim tam on myfitnesspal
[MS Paint] Original or double coat? Asking for a friend.
[Jimothy Wongingtons] @MS Paint: Gotta be double coat. There ain’t no going back to originals.
[try2bhelpful] @Jimothy Wongingtons: Tim Tam Deluxe Triple Choc or you are an amateur.
[peeppeep] @try2bhelpful: Doesn't go on half price as often :(
[TEER3X] Go one better and use AI to create meal plans and support for people. Profit.
[Drakesy] Was about to say just this
There's a reason no one's paying for this anymore
The relevance isn't there
[JustWantToSave] That's a lot of money for a site that gives you diet plans and health data tracking tools.
All of which can be found elsewhere for basically free.
If you're going to spend money on this kind of stuff, you're better off paying for a qualified and experienced expert to do proper measurements and such to them tailor make one for you (in person preferably).
You'll get far more accurate info.
[ASR-Briggs] No store in title. No price in title. What in the name of low effort
[Fitmusclebro] The “store” is CSIRO. $249 for 12 months
[ASR-Briggs] Cool. You’re meant to put that in the deal title. Just so you know.
[The Value] Just but the CSIRO cookbook for $40 at any good bookstore. It's what they use for the basis of their plan.
Unless you want to pay an extra $210 to access a forum.
[TEER3X] I don't really want to but anything. Each to their own though. No judgement here.
[Jimothy Wongingtons] Yeah but what if some huge discovery happens between when the book is printed and now? Like AI discovers that icecream for breakfast is beneficial? Or like… drinking 3 cans of monster a day is NOT excessive?
[wolfazrael123] You have a solid point. If something major may be after the printing of a book, it may also be discovered after a few years of following the most current advice today, and suggest that eating icecream is beneficial but you need to have 3 tubes in one hour.
[try2bhelpful] Go look at the local Op shop. You could probably get one for $3.
[M00Cow] I like the 5 food groups:
Pizza, Burgers, Burritos, Chicken and Sushi.
[M00Cow] The way this works is by emptying out your pockets
was $150 for black friday 2020 or $0 if you completed it.
https://www.ozbargain.com.au/node/586810
They're getting fat off the profits.
[Fitmusclebro] That was for a 12 week program, not 12 months.
[Dogstar] They're always trying to flog this on the Morning Show on Channel 7. There was a way to get it for free if it was successful but now it seems it's just an ongoing subscription like every other thing out there. As someone who recently lost 30kg, there's better options out there these days imo.
[Tunblor] What are your picks for the other options?
[anonym] This is OzBargain, not OzFreeAdvertising.
Actually saving yourself $699 on 12 month plan, that is 73% off!
I doubt anyone will actually pay full price on your overinflated RRP.
[c64] if any of these diet guides actually worked then everyone would be thin
[Headless] This should be free considering your tax dollars pays for the CSIRO…
